entities.summary:
Conrad of Gelnhausen was a German theologian and canon lawyer, one of the founders of the conciliar movement of the late fourteenth century.

Born in the Holy Roman Empire around 1370, Conrad was a key figure in the development of the conciliar movement, which sought to limit the power of the Pope and strengthen the authority of the Church.

In 1378, Conrad was elected Archbishop of Mainz, a position he held until his death in 1390. During his tenure, he played a crucial role in the election of several popes, including Gregory XI, and worked to promote the conciliar movement.

Conrad's significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as the conciliar movement laid the groundwork for the Protestant Reformation and the eventual rise of nation-states in Europe.

"The Church is not a thing to be obeyed, but a thing to be served," Conrad once said, reflecting the conciliar movement's emphasis on the Church's role as a servant of Christ.

This quote encapsulates Conrad's enduring legacy as a champion of Church reform and a precursor to the Protestant Reformation.
